option_description: Controls whether continuous on-access scanning is actively enabled and enforced by policy on the endpoint, intercepting files at the moment they are accessed, created, or executed rather than on a scheduled basis.
security_impact: The Rego policy flags a misconfiguration immediately if realtime_scanning_enabled is false, triggering the real_time_malware_detection_accuracy finding. Without on-access scanning, malicious files can execute before any detection occurs, rendering all other detection engine capabilities irrelevant. This is the foundational gate for the entire malware detection rule chain.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Log into the EPP/EDR management console (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne Management). Navigate to Devices > select the target workstation > Protection Status or Agent Health. Confirm 'Real-Time Protection' or 'On-Access Scanning' shows as Enabled or Active.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EPP Console > Devices > [Workstation Name] > Protection Status > Real-Time Protection
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Status field shows 'Enabled' or 'Active' with no policy exceptions listed for the device.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On a Windows endpoint, query Windows Defender or the installed AV agent via PowerShell to retrieve the real-time protection status directly from the local agent.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RealTimeProtectionEnabled: True, AMServiceEnabled: True

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the EPP management platform API for agent status. For Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, use the MDE API to retrieve device health state including real-time protection status.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response includes 'realTimeProtectionEnabled: true' and 'healthStatus: Active'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux endpoints running ClamAV with clamd or a third-party AV, check the service status and configuration to confirm on-access scanning is running.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Service shows 'active (running)' and OnAccessPrevention is set to 'yes'.

option_description: Captures the list of detection engine types currently active on the endpoint, such as signature-based, heuristic, and behavioral engines. Each engine type contributes a distinct detection capability layer against different malware categories.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires that at least one of 'heuristic' or 'behavioral' engines is present in addition to signature scanning. If only signature-based detection is active, the policy flags a misconfiguration because signature engines alone cannot detect zero-day threats, polymorphic malware, or fileless attacks. The policy logic checks: if realtime_scanning_enabled is true but neither 'heuristic' nor 'behavioral' appears in the detection_engines_active array, the finding triggers.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the EPP management console, navigate to the policy applied to the workstation and review the detection module settings. Look for sections labeled 'Detection Technologies', 'Protection Engines', or 'Scanning Options' and document which engine types are marked as enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EPP Console > Policies > [Applied Policy] > Detection Settings > Enabled Engines
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Checkboxes or toggles for Signature, Heuristic, and Behavioral analysis all show as enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows with Microsoft Defender, query the Defender preferences via PowerShell to identify which protection features and engine capabilities are active.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-MpPreference | Select-Object -Property DisableBehaviorMonitoring, DisableBlockAtFirstSeen, DisableIOAVProtection, DisableRealtimeMonitoring, MAPSReporting
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DisableBehaviorMonitoring: False, DisableBlockAtFirstSeen: False, DisableIOAVProtection: False — confirming behavioral and heuristic engines are active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For CrowdStrike Falcon, query the prevention policy API to retrieve configured detection modules for the host group or policy assigned to the workstation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response JSON lists prevention settings with 'cloud_anti_malware', 'behavioral', 'machine_learning', and 'sensor_anti_malware' modules showing 'enabled: true'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the endpoint security administrator to confirm which detection modules are licensed and enabled. Request the EPP vendor's feature matrix for the deployed product version to map licensed modules to engine types (signature, heuristic, behavioral).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Written confirmation or documentation showing all three engine types (signature, heuristic, behavioral) are licensed, deployed, and active in the production policy.

option_description: Records the number of days since the malware signature definitions were last successfully updated on the endpoint. Stale definitions mean the endpoint cannot detect malware variants published after the last update date.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers a real_time_malware_detection_accuracy finding if signature_definition_age_days exceeds 3, even when real-time scanning is enabled. This reflects the operational reality that threat actors publish new malware variants daily, and definitions older than 72 hours create a detection gap window. Endpoints disconnected from update infrastructure (e.g., remote workers, air-gapped machines) are particularly at risk of accumulating stale definitions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows endpoints, retrieve the last successful signature update timestamp from Windows Defender via PowerShell and calculate the age in days.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AntivirusSignatureAge: 0 or 1 (days), AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated: timestamp within last 24 hours.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the EPP management console, navigate to the device details page for the target workstation. Locate the 'Definition Version' or 'Last Updated' field under agent health information and compare the timestamp to the current date.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EPP Console > Devices > [Workstation Name] > Agent Health > Definition Last Updated
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Last Updated timestamp is within the last 1-3 days. Definitions older than 3 days require investigation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the EPP API for definition age data across all managed endpoints. For Microsoft Intune/MDE, use the device health status endpoint to retrieve signature update timestamps at scale.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON array with 'antimalwareSoftwareDefinitionUpdateTime' field; calculate current date minus this timestamp to derive age in days.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review Windows Event Log for Defender update events to determine last successful definition update. Filter for Event ID 2000 (successful update) and 2001 (update failed) in the Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational log.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' | Where-Object {$_.Id -in @(2000, 2001)} | Select-Object -First 10 TimeCreated, Id, Message
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Most recent Event ID 2000 entry shows a timestamp within the last 1-3 days. Presence of consecutive 2001 failures indicates update connectivity issues.

option_description: Controls whether tamper protection mechanisms are enabled to prevent unauthorized disabling, uninstalling, or modifying the endpoint protection agent and its configuration settings by local users or malicious processes.
security_impact: The Rego policy flags a misconfiguration if policy_tamper_protection_enabled is false even when real-time scanning is enabled. Without tamper protection, malware with local execution capability can disable AV services, delete definition files, or modify registry keys to blind the endpoint protection agent before executing its payload. This is a critical defense-in-depth layer because an endpoint with disabled AV and no tamper protection provides no detection capability regardless of policy configuration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows endpoints, check Windows Defender tamper protection status via PowerShell. This reflects both local configuration and MDM-enforced policy state.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IsTamperProtected: True; TamperProtection registry value: 5 (enabled and managed by Intune/MDM) or 1 (enabled locally).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Intune, navigate to Endpoint Security > Antivirus > [Policy Name] > Properties and confirm 'Enable Tamper Protection' is set to 'Enable'. For third-party EPP, check the vendor console's self-protection or tamper protection policy setting.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Intune Admin Center > Endpoint Security > Antivirus > [Policy] > Real-time Protection > Enable Tamper Protection: Enabled
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Tamper Protection setting is 'Enabled' and the policy is confirmed as applied to the target device or device group.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For CrowdStrike Falcon, query the prevention policy to confirm the 'Sensor Tamper Protection' module is enabled for the policy applied to the target workstation.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -X GET 'https://api.crowdstrike.com/policy/entities/prevention/v1?ids={policy_id}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {token}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; p=json.load(sys.stdin); print([s for s in p['resources'][0]['prevention_settings'] if 'tamper' in s['id'].lower()])"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON output shows tamper protection setting with 'enabled: true' for the applicable policy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Test tamper protection effectiveness by attempting to stop the AV service from an administrator account on a test endpoint. Confirm the operation is blocked with an access denied error.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Command returns 'Access is denied' or 'Cannot stop service' error, confirming tamper protection is actively blocking service termination attempts.

option_description: Identifies the security baseline framework applied to enforce hardened configuration on workstations. Valid options are CIS Benchmarks, DISA STIG, a custom organizational baseline, or none if no framework is applied.
security_impact: The Rego policy only awards the configuration_baseline_enforcement countermeasure when baseline_framework is not 'none'. A defined framework (cis, stig, or custom) signals that hardening controls are systematically applied rather than ad-hoc. Without a baseline framework, there is no structured reference to measure compliance against, making enforcement_mode and compliance_percentage meaningless. Organizations using 'none' have no systematic hardening posture and are exposed to default OS misconfigurations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Intune, navigate to Devices > Configuration Profiles and identify which compliance policy or security baseline profile is assigned to the workstation. Check the profile name and description for CIS or STIG references. In SCCM/Configuration Manager, check Compliance Settings > Configuration Baselines for assigned baselines.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Intune Admin Center > Devices > Configuration Profiles > [Profile Assigned to Device] > Properties > Description
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Profile name or description references 'CIS Benchmark', 'DISA STIG', or a named custom policy. No assigned baseline policy indicates value should be 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Intune-enrolled Windows devices via PowerShell with the Microsoft Graph API to retrieve applied configuration profiles and identify the baseline framework type from profile metadata.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-IntuneDeviceConfigurationPolicy | Where-Object {$_.displayName -match 'CIS|STIG|Baseline|Hardening'} | Select-Object displayName, lastModifiedDateTime, assignments
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Returns policy names containing baseline framework identifiers. Empty result suggests no recognized framework is assigned.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the Microsoft Graph API to list device configuration profiles assigned to a specific device and identify the baseline framework from profile display names.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON array of configuration states listing profile names; look for CIS, STIG, or custom baseline identifiers in 'displayName' fields.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the endpoint management team or review the IT security policy documentation to identify the official baseline framework decision. Request the configuration management plan or hardening standard document to confirm which framework is formally adopted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Written policy document or SOC/IT acknowledgment confirming the organization uses CIS Level 1/2, DISA STIG for Windows, or a named custom baseline derived from a recognized standard.

option_description: Determines whether the configuration baseline policy actively blocks and remediates unauthorized setting changes (enforce), only logs and alerts on violations without remediation (audit), or performs no active monitoring at all (disabled).
security_impact: The Rego policy requires enforcement_mode to equal 'enforce' for the configuration_baseline_enforcement countermeasure to be awarded. An 'audit' mode deployment still detects drift but allows misconfigured states to persist, meaning attackers or misconfigured software can operate in a weakened security posture indefinitely. 'Disabled' provides no protection. Only 'enforce' mode guarantees that unauthorized changes are actively reverted or blocked, preventing attackers from weakening security controls through configuration manipulation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Intune, check the compliance policy or configuration profile settings. Navigate to Endpoint Security > Security Baselines > [Baseline] > Properties to confirm the profile action. For non-compliant devices, check whether 'Mark device noncompliant' triggers automatic remediation actions or only reporting.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Intune Admin Center > Endpoint Security > Security Baselines > [Baseline Name] > Properties > Actions for Noncompliance
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Noncompliance actions show 'Retire', 'Wipe', or 'Block' configured with immediate or short-delay triggers, indicating enforce mode rather than audit-only.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the CIS-CAT Pro or SCAP scanner deployment configuration to determine whether it is running in remediation or audit-only mode. Check scheduled task parameters on a managed endpoint.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Task actions show command-line flags for the scanner; presence of '-r' or '--remediate' flags indicates enforce mode. Absence indicates audit-only.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Puppet or Ansible-based enforcement, query the configuration management API or run a dry-run check to determine whether the deployment is configured in enforce or noop (audit) mode.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If 'noop = true' appears in puppet.conf or the agent output, the deployment is in audit mode. Absence of noop flag and successful 'Applied catalog' messages confirm enforce mode.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the Ansible playbook or role configuration to determine whether the hardening role is deployed with check_mode enabled (audit) or in standard execution mode (enforce).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'check_mode: false' or absence of '--check' flags confirms enforce mode. Presence of 'check_mode: true' indicates audit-only deployment.

option_description: Represents the percentage of baseline security controls currently in a compliant state across managed endpoints, as measured by the configuration compliance scanning tool. A value of 100 means all checked controls meet the baseline; lower values indicate the proportion of failing controls.
security_impact: The Rego policy awards the configuration_baseline_enforcement countermeasure only when compliance_percentage is 90 or above (when combined with drift detection) or 95 or above (without drift detection). Values below these thresholds indicate that a material portion of hardening controls are failing — representing exploitable misconfigurations. Even in enforce mode, a low compliance percentage may indicate controls that cannot be auto-remediated, requiring manual intervention. Each percentage point below threshold represents specific hardening gaps attackers can leverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run CIS-CAT Pro Assessor against the target workstation or workstation group and review the HTML/JSON report summary. The overall compliance score percentage is displayed prominently in the report header and benchmark summary section.
how_to_obtain.navigation: CIS-CAT Pro Dashboard > Assessments > [Latest Assessment for Target] > Summary Score
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Numeric percentage score (e.g., 87%) with breakdown by CIS section. Target for this control is 90% minimum.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Microsoft Intune compliance reporting via PowerShell with the Microsoft Graph SDK to retrieve the device compliance state and calculate the overall percentage of compliant settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output groups compliance states (compliant, noncompliant, notApplicable) with counts. Calculate compliant/(compliant+noncompliant) * 100 for the compliance percentage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Tenable.sc or Tenable.io for the latest compliance scan results using the Tenable API to retrieve the compliance summary score for the workstation or workstation group.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response contains passed and failed control counts per host, allowing calculation of compliance percentage as passed/(passed+failed) * 100.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the Intune Device Compliance report in the Azure Portal to obtain current compliance percentage for the workstation fleet. Navigate to the compliance report export and identify overall pass rate.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal > Microsoft Intune > Reports > Device Compliance > Compliance Reports > All Devices Compliance
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Report shows per-device compliance status. Export to CSV and calculate the percentage of devices/settings marked 'Compliant' vs 'Not Compliant'.

option_description: Controls whether automated detection and alerting mechanisms are configured to identify when endpoint configurations deviate from the established security baseline, triggering alerts or remediation workflows when unauthorized changes are detected.
security_impact: The Rego policy uses drift_detection_enabled to differentiate between two passing thresholds: when drift detection is active, the compliance threshold for configuration_baseline_enforcement is 90%; without it, the threshold rises to 95%. This reflects that drift detection provides a compensating control — even if a setting briefly falls out of compliance, rapid detection and alerting limits the exposure window. Disabled drift detection means baseline violations may persist unnoticed indefinitely, silently eroding the hardening posture between scheduled scans.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Intune, navigate to Endpoint Security > Security Baselines > [Baseline] and verify that the baseline is assigned to device groups and that compliance check intervals are configured. In addition, check whether noncompliance notification rules and conditional access policies are active to confirm alerting is wired up.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Intune Admin Center > Endpoint Security > Security Baselines > [Baseline] > Assignments; also Reports > Monitor > Setting Compliance for active monitoring
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Baseline is assigned to all device groups, compliance checks run on a defined schedule (e.g., every 8 hours), and at least one noncompliance notification action is configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify that a configuration drift detection scheduled task or service is active on managed Windows endpoints, such as a recurring CIS-CAT scan task or Intune check-in task.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Task state shows 'Ready' with a NextRun time in the near future, confirming scheduled drift scanning is active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SIEM (e.g., Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel) API to verify that configuration drift detection alert rules are enabled and have fired recently, confirming the pipeline is active end-to-end.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Saved search or alert named for configuration drift is returned with 'is_scheduled: 1' and 'disabled: 0', confirming active monitoring.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the endpoint management team to confirm whether drift detection is configured as a continuous process (e.g., real-time MDM check-in) or periodic scan, and verify that alerts route to a monitored queue. Request evidence of a recent drift alert that was investigated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Team provides documentation or ticket evidence of a recent configuration drift alert, associated investigation record, and confirmation that alerts route to a SOC or IT security queue with defined response SLA.

option_description: Controls whether the endpoint agent's behavioral execution prevention module is actively loaded and enforcing policy. When enabled, the module monitors running processes for suspicious behaviors including code injection, privilege escalation attempts, and fileless attack techniques, blocking malicious actions in real time rather than relying solely on signature matching.
security_impact: The Rego policy immediately flags a misconfiguration if behavioral_protection_enabled is false, triggering the behavioral_execution_prevention finding at score 8 (high criticality). Without this enabled, the remaining prevention_mode and protection_capabilities checks are irrelevant — the entire behavioral prevention layer is absent, leaving endpoints exposed to memory-resident malware, LOLBin abuse, and injection-based attacks that evade signature detection.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Log in to the EPP/EDR management console (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, SentinelOne), navigate to Endpoints > Device Inventory, select the target workstation, and view the Agent Status or Policy Details pane. Confirm that the Behavioral Protection or Exploit Prevention module shows 'Enabled' or 'Active', not 'Disabled', 'Audit-only', or 'Unmanaged'.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Endpoints > Device Inventory > [Host] > Agent Status > Behavioral/Exploit Prevention Module
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Module status displays 'Enabled' or 'Active' with a green indicator

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows endpoints, query the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor registry key to check the behavioral protection state. A value of 1 for 'BehavioralProtectionMode' confirms enforcement is active.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: BehavioralProtectionMode    REG_DWORD    0x1

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, use PowerShell to query the real-time protection and behavior monitor status on the local agent.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object BehaviorMonitorEnabled, RealTimeProtectionEnabled, AMServiceEnabled | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: BehaviorMonitorEnabled : True  RealTimeProtectionEnabled : True  AMServiceEnabled : True

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the EDR management platform API to retrieve agent policy state. For CrowdStrike, use the Hosts API to fetch device details including prevention policy assignments and module states.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response showing prevention policy with behavioral_protection field as 'enabled' or 'active'

option_description: Defines the operational enforcement posture of the behavioral prevention engine — whether detected threats are actively blocked and terminated ('prevent'), passively alerted without intervention ('detect' or 'audit'), or the module is entirely inactive ('disabled'). This mode governs the actual blocking behavior for code injection, process hollowing, privilege escalation, and other behavioral detections.
security_impact: The Rego policy has a two-stage check: if behavioral_protection_enabled is true but prevention_mode is not 'prevent', the behavioral_execution_prevention finding is still triggered at score 8. Additionally, the automated_threat_response_coverage rule requires prevention_mode to equal 'enforce' (note: policy uses 'enforce' as equivalent intent) alongside automated_response_enabled and sufficient response actions. Deploying in 'detect' or 'audit' mode is a common operational pitfall — the agent observes attacks and logs them without stopping execution, providing a false sense of security.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the EPP/EDR management console, navigate to the Prevention Policy or Configuration Profile applied to the target workstation group. Locate the Behavioral Engine or Exploit Mitigation section and read the enforcement mode field. Common labels include 'Prevention Mode', 'Protection Level', or 'Policy Mode'.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Configuration > Prevention Policies > [Applied Policy] > Behavioral Engine Settings > Enforcement Mode
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mode field displays 'Prevent', 'Block', or 'Protect' — not 'Detect-only', 'Audit', or 'Monitor'

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows with SentinelOne, query the agent's operational mode via the Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) or the agent CLI tool.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output line showing 'protection_mode: protect' or equivalent prevention state

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Carbon Black CB Defense/App Control deployments, inspect the local sensor configuration XML to identify the current policy enforcement mode cached on the endpoint.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: sensorSettings entry with name 'PREVENTION_MODE' and value 'PREVENT' or '3'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve the prevention policy configuration via the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint API to confirm cloud-delivered protection and behavior blocking settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy object returned with behaviorMonitoringMode or cloudProtectionLevel showing block/prevent equivalent value

option_description: An explicit enumeration of the behavioral sub-modules currently active on the endpoint protection agent. Individual capabilities such as code injection prevention, privilege escalation blocking, fileless execution detection, and process hollowing prevention may be independently toggled within an overall behavioral policy, meaning the parent module can appear 'enabled' while critical sub-components are inactive.
security_impact: The Rego policy performs two granular array membership checks even when behavioral_protection_enabled is true and prevention_mode is 'prevent': it separately verifies that 'code_injection_prevention' is present in protection_capabilities AND that 'fileless_execution_detection' is present. Either omission independently triggers the behavioral_execution_prevention finding at score 8. This reflects real-world attack vectors — code injection is the primary persistence and lateral movement technique, while fileless attacks represent the fastest-growing evasion category.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the EPP/EDR management console, open the Prevention Policy applied to the target endpoint. Navigate to the Behavioral Protection or Exploit Mitigation sub-section and enumerate each individual toggle. Screenshot or export the full capability list noting which are 'On/Enabled' versus 'Off/Disabled'.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Configuration > Prevention Policies > [Policy Name] > Behavioral Protection > Individual Capability Toggles
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All critical capabilities — code_injection_prevention, privilege_escalation_blocking, fileless_execution_detection, process_hollowing_prevention — shown as Enabled/Active

how_to_obtain.instruction: For CrowdStrike Falcon, use the Falcon Prevention Policy API to retrieve the full prevention settings hash and identify which behavioral capabilities are set to true.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON array showing each behavioral capability group with enabled: true for code injection, fileless, and privilege escalation settings

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, query the locally active attack surface reduction (ASR) rules and controlled folder access state which map to behavioral capability sub-modules.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-MpPreference | Select-Object AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids, AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Actions, EnableControlledFolderAccess | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Actions array showing value '1' (block) for all rule IDs, not '2' (audit) or '0' (disabled)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For SentinelOne deployments, retrieve the policy details via the Management API to list all active mitigation modes per threat category.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: mitigationMode: 'protect' and populated array of active behavioral sub-policies including injection and fileless detection entries

option_description: Determines whether the endpoint protection platform autonomously executes containment actions — such as killing malicious processes, quarantining files, or isolating the host from the network — immediately upon a confirmed threat detection, without waiting for a security analyst to manually approve the response. When disabled, detections queue as alerts requiring human intervention before containment occurs.
security_impact: The Rego policy evaluates automated_threat_response_coverage as a countermeasure only when automated_response_enabled is true AND prevention_mode is 'enforce' AND at least two response actions are configured. If this attribute is false, the automated response countermeasure fails regardless of other settings. The business impact is mean-time-to-contain (MTTC): manual response workflows typically require 15–60 minutes, while automated containment can execute in under 10 seconds, directly limiting ransomware blast radius and lateral movement dwell time.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the EPP/EDR management console, navigate to the Response Policy or Incident Response configuration for the workstation's assigned policy group. Look for toggles labeled 'Automatic Remediation', 'Auto-Contain', 'Automated Response', or 'Active Response' and verify these are set to Enabled, not 'Detect Only' or 'Alert Only'.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Configuration > Response Policies > [Policy Name] > Automated Response Settings > Enable Automatic Containment
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Automated containment toggle shows Enabled/Active state; policy mode shows 'Protect' not 'Detect Only'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the CrowdStrike Falcon Response Policies API to confirm auto-containment settings are active for the policy applied to the target device.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON showing auto_remediation_enabled: true and containment_enabled: true

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, verify the automation level set for the device's device group via PowerShell using the MDE module, confirming 'Full - remediate threats automatically' rather than semi-automated or manual modes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AutomaticQuarantineEnabled : True indicating automated containment actions are permitted

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the IR runbook or EPP deployment configuration documentation to confirm that the approved operational posture explicitly enables automated response. Interview the endpoint security administrator to verify no change-control freeze or management directive has forced detection-only mode.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation confirms 'automated response: enabled' for production workstation policy group; no exceptions or overrides disabling auto-containment

option_description: Enumerates the specific automated containment actions that are armed and ready to execute upon threat detection within the endpoint protection policy. Individual response capabilities — process termination, file quarantine, host network isolation, and registry rollback — may each be independently configured, meaning automated response can be nominally enabled while only a subset of containment techniques are actually armed.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires count(response_actions_configured) >= 2 as part of the automated_threat_response_coverage countermeasure condition. This means a single configured action (e.g., only file quarantine without process termination) is insufficient to satisfy the rule. The rationale reflects defense-in-depth: process_termination stops active execution while file_quarantine prevents re-execution, and network_isolation contains lateral movement. An array with fewer than two entries leaves significant containment gaps even when automated response is nominally active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the EPP/EDR management console, open the Response Policy or Automated Response configuration section applied to the workstation. Enumerate each individual response action toggle — Process Kill/Terminate, File Quarantine, Network Isolation/Containment, Registry Rollback — and record which are in 'Enabled' or 'Active' state.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Configuration > Response Policies > [Policy Name] > Automated Actions > [Individual Action Toggles]
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At minimum process_termination and file_quarantine show Enabled; ideally network_isolation also enabled for high-severity detections

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SentinelOne Management API for the active threat response policy settings to enumerate all configured automated response actions for the target site or group.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H "Authorization: ApiToken <TOKEN>" "https://<console>/web/api/v2.1/groups?siteIds=<site_id>" | jq '.data[].registeredAt, .data[].inherits' && curl -s -H "Authorization: ApiToken <TOKEN>" "https://<console>/web/api/v2.1/policy?groupIds=<group_id>" | jq '.data | {autoMitigate: .autoMitigate, autoImmune: .autoImmune, networkQuarantine: .networkQuarantine}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON showing autoMitigate: true, and at least two of: quarantine, process kill, network isolation enabled

how_to_obtain.instruction: For CrowdStrike Falcon, retrieve the full response policy settings including all automated action configurations via the API and filter for response action entries.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" "https://api.crowdstrike.com/policy/entities/response/v1?ids=<policy_id>" | jq '[.resources[].settings.classes[] | select(.name | test("kill|quarantine|isolat|rollback"; "i")) | {action: .name, enabled: .enabled}]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Array of response action objects each showing enabled: true, with at least process kill and file quarantine present

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the EDR incident response logs for recent automatic containment events to empirically confirm which response actions have fired. This validates that configured actions are not just enabled in policy but are functionally executing.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' | Where-Object {$_.Id -in (1116,1117,1118,1119)} | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message | Format-List | Out-String | Select-String 'quarantine|terminate|isolat|contain'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Recent log entries showing automated quarantine and process termination events, confirming actions fire rather than just being policy-configured

option_description: Indicates whether the application control allowlisting engine is operating in active enforcement mode, blocking execution of any software not explicitly permitted by policy. When false or in audit/monitor-only mode, the application control policy logs violations but permits all execution, rendering the control ineffective as a defense against unauthorized software, malware droppers, and living-off-the-land binary abuse.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires allowlist_enforcement_enabled to be true before the application_control_whitelist_enforcement countermeasure can be awarded. An allowlisting solution deployed in audit mode is a common maturity gap — organizations enable it for visibility but defer enforcement due to fear of breaking legitimate applications, leaving the technical control functionally absent. This allows threat actors to execute arbitrary code including post-exploitation tools, ransomware payloads, and credential harvesters on endpoints where allowlisting is 'configured' but not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, check AppLocker enforcement state by querying the AppLocker policy. Enforcement mode 'Enabled' means blocking is active; 'AuditOnly' means violations are logged only.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective | Select-Object -ExpandProperty RuleCollections | Select-Object RuleCollectionType, EnforcementMode
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RuleCollectionType Exe with EnforcementMode 'Enabled'; Script and Msi collections also showing 'Enabled' not 'AuditOnly' or 'NotConfigured'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) enforcement state via the CodeIntegrity event log and CI policy status, confirming enforcement mode rather than audit.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-CIPolicy -FilePath "$env:SystemRoot\System32\CodeIntegrity\SiPolicy.p7b" 2>$null; Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-CodeIntegrity/Operational' -MaxEvents 10 | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, Message | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CI policy file present; Event ID 3077 (block in enforce mode) appearing rather than only 3076 (audit-mode blocks)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Carbon Black App Control or CrowdStrike Falcon Device Control, navigate to the application control policy applied to the target workstation and verify the enforcement mode indicator. Look for 'Enforcement Enabled', 'Lockdown Mode', or 'Enforcement Level: High/Full' settings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Configuration > App Control Policies > [Policy Name] > Enforcement Settings > Mode
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mode shows 'Enforce' or 'Block' rather than 'Monitor', 'Audit', or 'Report Only'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Group Policy Object (GPO) applied to the workstation to confirm AppLocker or SRP enforcement settings are configured and not overridden by local policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: GPO applying AppLocker or application control policy listed in Applied Group Policy Objects; no conflicting local policy override present

option_description: Defines the breadth of file types and execution contexts governed by the application control allowlist policy. 'Full' scope restricts executables (.exe), scripts (.ps1, .bat, .vbs, .js), installer packages (.msi, .msp), and dynamic libraries (.dll) across all execution contexts. 'Partial' scope typically covers only executables, leaving script execution and DLL sideloading uncontrolled. 'None' indicates no rules are configured despite the engine potentially being present.
security_impact: The Rego policy awards the application_control_whitelist_enforcement countermeasure for both 'full' and 'partial' enforcement_scope (when allowlist_enforcement_enabled is true and policy applies to standard users). However, 'partial' scope represents a significant residual risk: most modern malware delivery chains and post-exploitation frameworks (Cobalt Strike, Metasploit, PowerShell Empire) rely heavily on script execution — PowerShell, WScript, CScript — which partial policies leave unrestricted. 'None' combined with enabled enforcement indicates a broken or unconfigured policy state that provides no protection.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the full AppLocker rule set to determine which rule collection types have active rules. Collections with zero rules are unprotected execution categories.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective | Select-Object -ExpandProperty RuleCollections | ForEach-Object { [PSCustomObject]@{ Type=$_.RuleCollectionType; Mode=$_.EnforcementMode; RuleCount=($_.Rules | Measure-Object).Count } } | Format-Table -AutoSize
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Table showing all 5 rule types (Exe, Script, Msi, Appx, DLL) each with EnforcementMode 'Enabled' and RuleCount > 0 for full coverage; partial shows only Exe with rules

how_to_obtain.instruction: For WDAC policies, decode the applied policy XML to identify which file rule levels and signing scenarios are covered, revealing whether scripts and DLLs are in scope.
how_to_obtain.command: ConvertFrom-CIPolicy -XmlFilePath "$env:SystemRoot\System32\CodeIntegrity\CIPolicies\Active\*.xml" | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FileRules | Group-Object -Property Type | Select-Object Name, Count
how_to_obtain.expected_output: FileRule types including 'Allow' rules for both executables and scripts present; DLL enforcement rules present for full scope

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the application control management console (Carbon Black App Control, Airlock Digital, or similar), view the active ruleset categories applied to the target policy. Verify coverage includes executables, scripts (all interpreter types), installer packages, and optionally DLLs.
how_to_obtain.navigation: App Control > Policies > [Policy Name] > Rules > File Categories Covered
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All four major execution categories (executables, scripts, installers, libraries) show active rules with block-by-default posture for full scope; only executables visible for partial

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review AppLocker or WDAC event logs for blocked execution attempts across different file type categories. Presence of script-type block events (Event ID 8006 for script rules) alongside executable blocks confirms script scope coverage.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/MSI and Script' -MaxEvents 50 | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, Message | Format-List; Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/EXE and DLL' -MaxEvents 50 | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, Message | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Events present in both the 'MSI and Script' and 'EXE and DLL' AppLocker logs with enforcement mode blocks (not just audit events), confirming full scope enforcement

option_description: Controls whether the application allowlist/denylist enforcement policy is scoped to include standard (non-administrator) user accounts. When false, only administrator accounts may be subject to application control rules, leaving standard users unprotected or unrestricted.
security_impact: The Rego policy for application_control_whitelist_enforcement only fires the countermeasure when policy_applies_to_standard_users == true, regardless of whether enforcement_scope is 'full' or 'partial'. Without this attribute set to true, the control provides no credit even if allowlisting is technically enabled, because the users most likely to execute malicious payloads (standard users) are not covered.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, query AppLocker policy to verify rule scope targets 'Everyone' or specific standard-user groups using PowerShell.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output should show UserOrGroupSid='S-1-1-0' (Everyone) or a SID corresponding to a standard user group in each rule block.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Windows Group Policy Management Console (GPMC), navigate to the AppLocker or Software Restriction Policies configuration and inspect each rule's 'User or Group' column to confirm standard users are included.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Group Policy Management Console → Forest → Domains → [Domain] → Group Policy Objects → [EPP Policy] → Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Application Control Policies → AppLocker → [Rule Type] → review 'User or Group' column
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'Everyone' or a standard user group (e.g., 'DOMAIN\Domain Users') appears in rule assignments.

how_to_obtain.instruction: If using a third-party endpoint protection agent (e.g., Carbon Black, CrowdStrike), inspect the exported policy JSON or XML for user-scope fields.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy object should contain a user_scope or target_users field referencing non-admin user groups.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query your endpoint management platform API (e.g., Microsoft Intune) to retrieve the assigned application control profile and inspect scope assignments.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response shows assignments targeting 'All Users' or a group that includes standard users, not scoped exclusively to admin accounts.

option_description: Indicates whether the endpoint protection agent has comprehensive telemetry collection activated, covering process creation events, file operations, registry changes, and network connection data. This is the master switch that must be true before individual event type coverage is meaningful.
security_impact: In the Rego policy, telemetry_and_logging_completeness requires telemetry_logging_enabled == true as a precondition in both rule branches before evaluating event type coverage and SIEM integration status. If this flag is false, the telemetry completeness countermeasure cannot fire regardless of what event types are configured, leaving the organization without endpoint audit trails for forensic investigation or SIEM correlation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open the endpoint protection management console (e.g., Microsoft Defender Security Center, CrowdStrike Falcon console, or Carbon Black Cloud) and navigate to the device's policy assignment to confirm telemetry/audit logging is enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Endpoint Console → Devices → [Select Device] → Policy Details → Logging & Telemetry → verify 'Event Logging' or 'Telemetry Collection' is toggled ON
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Telemetry or event logging toggle shows 'Enabled' or equivalent active state.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows endpoints using Microsoft Defender, check the telemetry and data collection level via PowerShell registry query.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection' -Name 'AllowTelemetry' | Select-Object AllowTelemetry; Get-MpPreference | Select-Object DisableRealtimeMonitoring, EnableNetworkProtection
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AllowTelemetry value of 1, 2, or 3 indicates telemetry enabled; DisableRealtimeMonitoring should be False.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the EDR platform API to retrieve agent configuration and confirm telemetry is active for a specific device.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response returns true for telemetry_enabled or logging_enabled fields.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify telemetry is actively generating events by checking local agent logs or SIEM for recent process creation and file operation events from this endpoint.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' -MaxEvents 20 | Where-Object { $_.Id -in 1,3,11,13 } | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, Message
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Recent events (within the last hour) for event IDs 1 (process create), 3 (network), 11 (file create), 13 (registry) confirm active telemetry.

option_description: An array listing which specific endpoint event categories are actively collected and forwarded by the endpoint protection agent. The expected comprehensive set includes process_creation, file_operations, registry_changes, and network_connections. Gaps in this list represent blind spots in endpoint visibility.
security_impact: The Rego telemetry_and_logging_completeness rule has two branches with different event type requirements. The first branch (qualifying for active SIEM status) requires at minimum process_creation, file_operations, and network_connections. The stricter second branch (for configured_not_verified SIEM status) requires all four types including registry_changes. Missing any required event type from this array prevents the corresponding rule branch from satisfying the countermeasure, reducing forensic and detection coverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the endpoint protection management console, navigate to the active telemetry policy and enumerate each enabled event category checkbox or toggle.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Endpoint Console → Policies → [Active Policy] → Telemetry Settings → Event Categories → review which categories are checked: Process Creation, File Operations, Registry Changes, Network Connections
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All four categories (or at minimum three) are shown as enabled in the policy configuration view.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows with Sysmon deployed as the telemetry agent, inspect the active Sysmon configuration to enumerate monitored event types.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output lists event types with their enabled/disabled state; all four core categories should appear as 'enabled'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the Sysmon XML configuration file or endpoint agent policy file to extract the list of active event collection rules.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: XML elements for each expected event type are present and not commented out or set to onmatch='exclude' without inclusions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the SIEM for recent event ingestion by querying for each expected event type from this endpoint over the past 24 hours.
how_to_obtain.command: index=endpoint_logs host="<workstation_hostname>" | stats count by event_type | where event_type IN ("process_creation","file_operations","registry_changes","network_connections")
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each of the four event types shows a nonzero count of events ingested within the past 24 hours.

option_description: Describes the operational state of the endpoint telemetry forwarding pipeline to a centralized SIEM or log management platform. The enum progresses from not_configured (no setup) through disabled and configured_not_verified to active (verified bidirectional flow of events).
security_impact: The Rego policy references this attribute in both telemetry_and_logging_completeness and siem_and_edr_integration_depth rules. For telemetry completeness, the first rule branch (requiring only three event types) requires siem_integration_status == 'active', while the stricter branch allows 'configured_not_verified' but mandates all four event types. For siem_and_edr_integration_depth, the Rego checks siem_integration_status == true (boolean cast), meaning only 'active' satisfies the condition. Any status other than 'active' degrades or eliminates credit for both countermeasures.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the endpoint protection management console, navigate to SIEM integration or log forwarding settings and check the connection status indicator.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Endpoint Console → Integrations → SIEM / Log Forwarding → review connection status badge (Active / Error / Not Configured) and last successful event timestamp
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Status indicator shows 'Active' or 'Connected' with a recent last-event timestamp (within the past hour).

how_to_obtain.instruction: From the endpoint or forwarder host, test TCP connectivity to the SIEM ingestion endpoint to confirm network path is open.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TcpTestSucceeded returns True for the configured syslog or encrypted syslog port.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SIEM for recent events from this endpoint to confirm active ingestion rather than relying solely on console status.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Count > 0 events received from the target host within the last hour, confirming active forwarding.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the local log forwarder (e.g., Winlogbeat, NXLog, or Splunk UF) service status and review its own logs for forwarding errors.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Service status is 'Running' and logs show successful connection messages without recent error entries.

option_description: Represents the health and connectivity state of the API link between the endpoint protection platform and the organization's EDR or XDR platform. This integration enables bidirectional alert sharing, automated response orchestration, and correlated threat context across tools.
security_impact: The Rego siem_and_edr_integration_depth rule requires edr_api_integration_status == 'active' in both of its branches. A status of 'degraded', 'disabled', or 'misconfigured' prevents the EDR integration depth countermeasure from firing entirely. This means correlated detection capabilities and automated response playbooks that depend on the API link are considered non-functional from a security posture perspective.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open the EDR/XDR platform management console and verify the endpoint protection integration connector shows an active status with recent heartbeat.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EDR Console → Settings → Integrations → Endpoint Protection → [Connected Platform] → verify Connection Status is 'Active' and Last Sync timestamp is recent
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Integration tile shows green 'Active' status with a last-sync timestamp within the past 15 minutes.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the EDR platform REST API to check the integration health endpoint and confirm connectivity status.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response returns status: 'active' and a last_heartbeat timestamp within the past few minutes; error_message should be null.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Test reachability to the EDR API endpoint from the integration host to rule out network-layer connectivity issues.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 200 response with a healthy status body confirms API endpoint is reachable and credentials are valid.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the EDR integration connector logs for authentication failures, timeout errors, or certificate issues that would indicate a misconfigured or degraded state.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log shows 'Successfully connected' or 'Heartbeat sent' entries without authentication or timeout errors in the recent entries.

option_description: Determines whether endpoint security alerts forwarded to the SIEM are augmented with contextual metadata fields such as asset owner, hostname, business unit, and threat intelligence tags. Enrichment transforms raw alerts into actionable, correlated detections by providing analysts with immediate context.
security_impact: The Rego siem_and_edr_integration_depth rule's first branch includes alert_enrichment_configured == true as an additional qualifying condition alongside active SIEM and EDR API integration. While the second branch can satisfy the rule without enrichment, having enrichment true improves detection quality and satisfies the more complete integration scenario. Without enrichment, analysts face decontextualized alerts that increase investigation time and reduce detection efficacy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the SIEM ingestion pipeline or parsing rules to confirm enrichment fields are being appended to endpoint alert events.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM Console → Settings → Data Inputs → Endpoint Protection Source → Field Extraction / Enrichment Rules → verify asset_owner, hostname, and threat_intel_tags fields are mapped
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enrichment rules show mappings for at least asset classification, hostname, and threat intelligence tag fields applied to endpoint alert events.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search the SIEM for a recent endpoint alert and inspect the raw event to verify enrichment fields are present.
how_to_obtain.command: index=endpoint_alerts | head 5 | table _time, host, asset_owner, threat_intel_tags, severity, event_type
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Query results show populated asset_owner and threat_intel_tags fields alongside standard event fields in recent alert records.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the log forwarder or SIEM connector configuration file for enrichment field definitions or lookup table references.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration contains filter blocks with enrich, lookup, or mutate directives adding asset and threat intelligence context fields.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve a sample alert via the SIEM API and validate that enrichment metadata fields are present in the response payload.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <siem_token>' 'https://<siem>/api/v1/alerts?source=endpoint&limit=1' | jq '.alerts[0] | {asset_owner, hostname, threat_intel_tags, business_unit}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response includes non-null values for asset_owner, hostname, and threat_intel_tags fields in the alert record.

option_description: Controls whether the endpoint protection agent is configured to automatically pull and apply updated malware signatures and detection definitions from the configured update source. This covers both the enablement of automatic updates and the reachability of the update server.
security_impact: The Rego signature_update_and_definition_currency rule requires signature_update_enabled == true as its first condition before evaluating signature freshness (age <= 24 hours) and update source reachability. If auto-update is disabled, the signature currency countermeasure cannot fire even if definitions happen to be current, because there is no mechanism ensuring they will remain current. Stale signatures directly reduce detection rates for known malware families.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows with Microsoft Defender, check the automatic update configuration and MU/WU client settings via PowerShell.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-MpPreference | Select-Object SignatureDisableUpdateOnStartupWithoutEngine, SignatureUpdateInterval, SignatureUpdateCatchupInterval; Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates' | Select-Object SignatureUpdateInterval, FallbackOrder
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SignatureUpdateInterval is set to a nonzero value (e.g., 1–8 hours); FallbackOrder lists valid update sources.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the endpoint protection management console, open the policy assigned to the device and confirm the signature update schedule is enabled with a defined frequency.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Endpoint Console → Policies → [Active Policy] → Updates → Signature / Definition Updates → verify 'Automatic Updates' is enabled and update frequency is configured (e.g., every 4 hours)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Automatic updates toggle is ON and update interval shows a configured frequency of 24 hours or less.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify that the endpoint can reach the configured signature update server to confirm the update source is reachable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TcpTestSucceeded returns True for each update server, confirming network path is open for definition downloads.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Windows Event Log or agent logs for recent successful signature update events to confirm updates are actively occurring.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'System' | Where-Object { $_.Id -in 1001,1002 -and $_.ProviderName -like '*Defender*' } | Select-Object -First 5 TimeCreated, Message; Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated timestamp is within the past 24 hours and event log shows successful update completion events.

option_description: An integer representing the number of hours that have elapsed since the last successful signature or definition update was applied to the endpoint protection agent. Lower values indicate fresher, more current threat detection capability. A value of 0 would indicate a very recent update.
security_impact: The Rego signature_update_and_definition_currency rule enforces signature_age_hours <= 24 as a hard threshold. Signatures older than 24 hours fail this condition and the countermeasure does not fire, reflecting the operational risk that recently published malware variants—for which definitions exist in the vendor cloud—will not be detected on the endpoint. In active threat environments, even 24-hour-old signatures may miss rapidly propagating ransomware or zero-day campaigns where vendors publish definitions within hours.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows with Microsoft Defender, retrieve the last update timestamp and calculate elapsed hours via PowerShell.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output displays the last update timestamp and a calculated age in hours; value should be 24 or less for a compliant endpoint.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the endpoint protection management console, navigate to the device detail view and locate the signature version and last update timestamp fields.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Endpoint Console → Devices → [Select Device] → Agent Details → Signature Version / Last Definition Update → note the timestamp and calculate elapsed time
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Last Definition Update field shows a timestamp within the past 24 hours; signature version matches the vendor's current published version.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the endpoint management platform API to retrieve the signature age for a specific device programmatically.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response returns an ISO 8601 timestamp; calculate the difference from the current UTC time to derive hours elapsed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search SIEM or endpoint telemetry logs for the most recent signature update success event from the target host to determine last update time.
how_to_obtain.command: index=endpoint_logs host="<workstation_hostname>" event_type="signature_update" status="success" | sort -_time | head 1 | table _time, signature_version, update_source
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Most recent successful update event timestamp; compute difference from current time to determine signature age in hours.

option_description: Controls whether the workstation endpoint protection agent can successfully communicate with its configured signature update source, which may be a vendor cloud service (e.g., Symantec LiveUpdate, Microsoft Update), an internal WSUS server, or an on-premises mirror server. This attribute reflects real-time network connectivity status between the agent and its update infrastructure.
security_impact: The Rego policy rule 'signature_update_and_definition_currency' fires the countermeasure only when update_source_reachable is true, signature updates are enabled, and signature age is within 24 hours. If the update source is unreachable, the agent cannot pull fresh definitions regardless of scheduling configuration, causing signature staleness that will breach the 24-hour freshness threshold and disqualify the endpoint from contributing to the Signature Update And Definition Currency countermeasure. Stale signatures leave the endpoint blind to recently discovered malware variants.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From the endpoint, attempt a direct TCP connectivity test to the configured update server hostname or IP on port 80/443 (or 8530/8531 for WSUS). This confirms whether the network path is open.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TcpTestSucceeded: True indicates the endpoint can reach the update source; False or timeout indicates a blocked or unreachable path.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the endpoint protection agent log file for update attempt results, looking for 'update source unreachable', 'connection failed', or 'last successful update' timestamps that are older than 24 hours.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines showing successful connection timestamps within the last 24 hours; absence of 'unreachable' or 'connection refused' errors.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the centralized endpoint protection management console, navigate to the agent health or update status dashboard and filter for agents showing 'Update Source Unreachable' or 'Last Contact' alerts older than 24 hours.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Management Console → Reports → Agent Health → Filter: Update Status = 'Source Unreachable' or Last Update > 24h ago
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Zero agents listed under unreachable update source status; all agents show a last successful update timestamp within 24 hours.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows endpoints using WSUS, query the Windows Update client to identify the configured update server and test reachability using the wuauclt or UsoClient utility.
how_to_obtain.command: reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate /v WUServer && curl -I $(reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate /v WUServer | findstr WUServer | awk '{print $3}')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 200 or 400 response from the WSUS server URL confirms network reachability; connection refused or timeout indicates the source is unreachable.

typical_values: true (majority of managed endpoints in well-maintained environments)
false (common for laptops off-VPN, air-gapped segments, or misconfigured proxy environments)

option_description: Indicates whether the endpoint protection management console is actively running and whether workstation agents are enrolled and reporting status back to it. This covers both the console service availability and the agent-to-console enrollment relationship, which is the foundation for centralized policy management, health monitoring, and exception handling across the workstation fleet.
security_impact: The Rego policy rule 'operational_policy_maintainability' requires centralized_console_enabled to be true as the primary gate before evaluating policy_deployment_status and unhealthy_agent_percentage. Without an active console, there is no mechanism to verify consistent policy application, monitor agent health, or detect configuration drift across the fleet. The Operational Policy Maintainability countermeasure cannot be satisfied without this prerequisite, leaving administrators unable to enforce or audit security posture at scale.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Log into the endpoint protection management console web interface and verify the dashboard loads successfully, displays enrolled agent counts, and shows agents in a 'Managed' or 'Connected' state rather than showing service errors.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EPP Management Console URL → Dashboard → Overview → Agent Enrollment Summary (e.g., Symantec SEPM: https://<sepm-server>:8443/console, CrowdStrike Falcon: https://falcon.crowdstrike.com, Defender for Endpoint: https://security.microsoft.com)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Console loads without errors; enrolled agent count matches expected fleet size; agents appear with 'Online' or 'Managed' status.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the management server, check whether the console service processes are running using the system service manager.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Status: Running; StartType: Automatic. A stopped or degraded service indicates the console is not operational.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the EPP management console REST API health endpoint to confirm the service is active and agents are reporting. Example shown for a generic EPP REST API pattern; substitute vendor-specific endpoint.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response with status: 'healthy' or 'operational' and agent_count greater than zero confirms the console is enabled and agents are enrolled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the endpoint security administrator to confirm whether a management console was deployed as part of the EPP rollout, whether agents were enrolled during deployment, and whether console availability is monitored via NOC alerts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Administrator confirms console is deployed, agent enrollment process was completed for all workstations, and console uptime is monitored.

typical_values: true (standard in enterprise deployments with dedicated EPP infrastructure)
false (common in SMB environments using standalone agents, or when the console server has failed without alerting)

option_description: Reflects the current state of security policy distribution from the centralized management console to the managed endpoint fleet. A 'fully_deployed' status means all enrolled agents have received and applied the current active policy set. 'Partially_deployed' indicates a subset of agents has not yet received or applied policies. 'Not_deployed' means no policy has been pushed. 'Unknown' reflects a state where the console cannot determine deployment completeness, often due to agent communication failures.
security_impact: The Rego policy rule 'operational_policy_maintainability' requires policy_deployment_status to equal 'fully_deployed' (combined with console enabled and unhealthy agent percentage at or below 5%) to satisfy the countermeasure. Any status other than 'fully_deployed' means portions of the workstation fleet are operating under outdated, incomplete, or unknown policy configurations, creating inconsistent security posture. Endpoints with stale or missing policies may lack critical detections, tamper protection settings, or behavioral rules that the organization believes are universally applied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the management console, navigate to the policy deployment or compliance dashboard to view a per-policy deployment report showing which endpoints have applied the current policy version versus those with pending or failed deployments.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EPP Console → Policies → Deployment Status → View All → Filter by Policy Version = Current; check 'Pending', 'Failed', or 'Not Applied' counts (e.g., in SEPM: Admin → Policies → Policy Summary; in Defender: Intune → Endpoint Security → Policy Assignment Status)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All enrolled endpoints show 'Applied' or 'Compliant' against the current policy version; zero endpoints in 'Pending' or 'Failed' state indicates fully_deployed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the management console API for a policy compliance report to retrieve deployment status programmatically, which can be used for automated assessments.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response with a 'deployment_status' field showing 'fully_deployed', or a breakdown of applied_count vs total_count where applied_count equals total_count.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft Defender environments managed via Intune, use the Microsoft Graph API or PowerShell SDK to retrieve policy assignment and compliance status across the device fleet.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All'; Get-MgDeviceManagementDeviceCompliancePolicyDeviceStateSummary | Select-Object CompliantDeviceCount, NonCompliantDeviceCount, PendingCount, ErrorCount
how_to_obtain.expected_output: NonCompliantDeviceCount = 0, PendingCount = 0, ErrorCount = 0 alongside a CompliantDeviceCount matching total enrolled devices indicates fully_deployed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the management console event or audit logs for policy push events, looking for failed deployments, timeout errors, or partial application records that would indicate partially_deployed or not_deployed status.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No recent failure or timeout entries; last policy push log entries show successful completion for all target agent groups.

typical_values: fully_deployed (target state for mature environments with stable agent connectivity)
partially_deployed (common in large enterprises with laptops intermittently off-network or agents pending restart)
unknown (frequently seen when the console has stale agent records or agents have been offline for extended periods)
not_deployed (typically only in newly stood-up environments or following a console migration)

option_description: Represents the proportion of enrolled workstation agents that are in a degraded operational state, expressed as a percentage of the total enrolled agent population. An agent is considered unhealthy if it is offline (no check-in within the console's configured interval), out-of-policy (running an older policy version than currently active), tamper-detected (agent files or services modified), or reporting internal errors. Calculated as (unhealthy_or_offline_agents / total_enrolled_agents) * 100.
security_impact: The Rego policy rule 'operational_policy_maintainability' enforces a threshold of unhealthy_agent_percentage <= 5 as a condition for satisfying the countermeasure. Agents above this threshold indicate a meaningful fraction of the fleet is operating without verified protection, current policies, or active threat detection. Even at 10% unhealthy in a 1,000-workstation fleet, 100 endpoints are unprotected and invisible to the management plane, creating significant blind spots for malware propagation and policy enforcement gaps.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Access the management console agent health dashboard and identify the total enrolled agent count alongside counts for offline, out-of-policy, and error-state agents. Calculate the percentage manually or use the console's built-in compliance percentage widget.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EPP Console → Dashboard → Agent Health Summary → View: Unhealthy/Offline Agents; note 'Total Enrolled' vs 'Healthy' counts and compute (Unhealthy / Total) * 100 (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon: Host Management → Filter: Status = Reduced Functionality; Defender: Security.microsoft.com → Devices → Filter: Health State = Inactive or At Risk)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A percentage value at or below 5% indicates acceptable fleet health; values above 5% trigger the policy condition. Dashboard may display this directly as a health score or compliance percentage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the EPP management API for agent health statistics to retrieve counts of healthy versus unhealthy agents programmatically, enabling automated threshold evaluation.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>' 'https://<console-host>/api/v1/agents/health-summary' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Unhealthy%: {round((d[\"unhealthy_count\"]/d[\"total_enrolled\"])*100,2)}')"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output showing unhealthy percentage; value of 0-5 is compliant with the Rego policy threshold; values above 5 indicate remediation is needed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For environments using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, use the Microsoft Graph Security API to enumerate devices by health status and calculate the unhealthy percentage from device risk and onboarding state fields.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'SecurityEvents.Read.All'; $devices = Get-MgSecurityAlert; $total = (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$count=true' -OutputType PSObject).value.Count; $unhealthy = (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?`$filter=complianceState ne 'compliant'&`$count=true" -OutputType PSObject).value.Count; Write-Host "Unhealthy%: $([math]::Round(($unhealthy/$total)*100,2))"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A printed percentage value; 0-5% is within the acceptable threshold defined by the Rego policy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the management console's agent check-in logs and error logs to identify agents that have not communicated within the configured heartbeat interval, which typically defines 'offline' status.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-Content 'C:\Program Files\<EPP_Console>\logs\agent-checkin.log' | Where-Object { $_ -match 'last_seen|offline|error|tamper' } | Select-String -Pattern '(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})' | Group-Object | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object -First 20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Entries showing agents with last-seen timestamps beyond the heartbeat threshold (commonly 15-30 minutes) confirm offline/unhealthy status; minimal such entries indicate low unhealthy agent percentage.

typical_values: 0 (ideal state; all agents healthy and reporting)
1-5 (acceptable range; typically reflects laptops temporarily off-network or pending reboots)
6-15 (common in organizations with poor agent lifecycle management or frequent OS reimaging without re-enrollment)
16-40 (indicates systemic issues such as console connectivity problems, mass agent corruption, or large unmanaged device populations)
